text:
anya: Quick sync — we have 3 customer asks: 1) API-only model pinning for infra teams, 2) Console rollout UI for product owners, 3) per-route cost controls. How do we prioritize?

mike: tl;dr: API-first gets us fastest time-to-value and fewer UI edge cases. Console work is larger surface area and has many UX iterations.

sara: Devex input: onboarding friction is the main blocker for second-wave customers. They try API, hit auth/roles, give up. A lightweight console could reduce churn.

tom: From SEs — customers ask for console controls during procurement. They need visible SLA/cost controls to sign. So Console has revenue impact for enterprise deals.

leo: Suggest we use a RICE-ish approach, but tweak "Reach" to count procurement decision-makers too. Can we do a quick scoring and sequence?

mike: Agree. Also factor in implementation risk: console implies server-side feature flags, more telemetry, and copywriting. API pinning is straightforward.

anya: I'm proposing two phases: Phase A = API-first with an admin CLI + docs + example console mockups. Phase B = Minimal Console (pin + cost) for sales plays. Sequence by bet size and launch criteria. Thoughts?

tom: +1 for sales plays. But we need acceptance criteria: can SEs demo without a full console? If not, risk to deals.

sara: Demoable surface could be a hosted admin page that reads from the same API — much smaller than a full Console. That reduces dev work and keeps API the source-of-truth.

leo: Let's do a quick RICE table in thread:
```
Feature                 Reach   Impact   Confidence   Effort   RICE score
API model pinning         8      7        0.8         2        224
Hosted admin demo         6      6        0.7         3        84
Full Console rollout      4      9        0.6         8        27
Per-route cost controls   5      7        0.7         4        61
```
(rough numbers)

mike: Those numbers line up with engineering intuition. API pinning first, hosted admin for sales, then iterate console.

anya: Launch criteria idea for Phase A (API-first):
- API contract stable and documented
- SDK examples + auth recipes
- SE demo flow available (hosted admin or scripted demo)
- Perf targets validated for pinned models

tom: Also add: revenue trigger for moving to Phase B (e.g., three Enterprise deals stalled for lack of visible controls).

sara: Can we reduce Console scope? Start with a read-only view + pin + basic cost slider instead of full policy editor. That hits procurement and reduces complexity.

mike: Implementation notes: reuse existing perms model, surface a small admin route in private control plane for hosted demos, and add telemetry hooks for cost signals. Avoid building reusable UI components until we validate demand.

leo: Product ask: set a 6-week sprint to ship Phase A MVP. If metrics (onboarding conversion and SE win rate) improve by X, greenlight Phase B.

anya: Sounds good. Action items:
- mike: scoping + rough estimate for API pinning + hosted admin (due EOD fri)
- sara: write onboarding checklist and demo script for SEs (Mon)
- tom: collect 3 current deals that would benefit from console visibility (today)
- leo: draft RICE doc and measurable success metrics (Mon)

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline queued for branch feature/api-model-pinning (CI passed) :rocket:

mike: will do the scoping. Quick Q: do we want a canary flag for the admin route? safer to toggle.

anya: yes — canary + permission gated. Keep rollout tight.

tom: :thumbsup:

sara: adding a short user survey to onboarding flow to capture whether admin/ui would have helped them (2 questions).

anya: Great. If we all agree, I'll add this sequence to the roadmap doc and mark Console as conditional on metrics.

leo: agreed.

mike: agreed.

tom: agreed.

sara: agreed.

anya: thanks everyone — will update the roadmap and ping for the sync notes.
